sources.entry: OpenHands - Open-source platform for autonomous AI software development agents that can write code, fix bugs, and run shell commands. #free #opensource

summary.one_liner: Agent Canvas is a self-hosted control center from the OpenHands project for running coding agents (OpenHands, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Pi, OpenCode, or any ACP-compatible agent) locally, in Docker, on VMs, or in the cloud, with Slack/GitHub-triggered automations.
use_cases: Run coding agents on a laptop, dedicated machine, or cloud server
Automate scheduled reports that publish to Slack
Decompose GitHub issues into tasks automatically
Run several agents concurrently in separate Docker containers
Share an agent server with a team for code review and dependency updates
Switch one UI between local, remote, and cloud agent backends
how_to_run: git clone <repo> && cd OpenHands && npm ci && npm run dev
stack: Python agent server (OpenHands Agent Server / software-agent-sdk)
notable: Runs the open-source OpenHands agent out of the box and also drives third-party agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Pi, and OpenCode
One frontend can connect to multiple agent server backends (laptop, Docker, VM, company infrastructure) and switch between them
Optional Docker mode runs each conversation in its own container with its own Agent Server
Automations run on a schedule or in response to webhook events, integrating with Slack, GitHub, Linear, and Notion
Local listeners bind to loopback by default; session key handling is explicit for LAN exposure
caveats: The npm and source launchers run the agent server directly on the host, giving the agent full filesystem access; only the Docker sandbox options isolate execution
Docker-per-conversation mode isolates conversation execution only; the Canvas and automation service are not sandboxed
Existing local conversations are not converted when switching to Docker mode
Source install requires npm 11.12.1 pin and a git clone; Windows users are pointed to a separate README.windows.md
Internet-facing installs need additional hardening per the self-hosting guide
